subject.title: Create Claw agent and root install record

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this plan-integrity consent model and shared root-provenance ledger as the supported mutating second slice of the Claws RFC?
rationale: The code appears mechanically sound after the latest repairs, but it creates a new core CLI lifecycle, persistent data model, consent contract, and future ownership obligations that cannot be accepted through automated correctness review alone.

options.title: Approve the RFC slice
options.body: Accept the consent and ledger model, then require a clean restack plus upgrade and recovery proof before merge.

options.title: Keep Claws read-only
options.body: Proceed only with inspection and planning while deferring all config, workspace, and persistent-state mutation.

options.title: Reject core lifecycle ownership
options.body: Close the mutation stack if grouped Claw installation and lifecycle state should not be owned by OpenClaw core.

recommendation.title: Approve the RFC slice
recommendation.body: Accept the consent and ledger model, then require a clean restack plus upgrade and recovery proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The available timeline connects this person to the RFC stack, and the unresolved choice is core product and lifecycle direction rather than a mechanical code repair.
